questions.q: Why must every event subscriber be designed to tolerate duplicate delivery?
options: Because duplicate delivery is a rare bug that only happens in sandbox orgs
Because at-least-once delivery is the platform's actual documented guarantee, not an unlikely edge case
Because platform events always deliver each event exactly three times
Because duplicates only occur with standard-volume events, never high-volume ones
questions.explain: At-least-once delivery is the platform's stated contract, meaning duplicate delivery is an expected, designed-for occurrence — not a rare failure a subscriber can safely ignore.

questions.q: Which of these operations is naturally idempotent?
options: INSERT a new Shipment_Log__c record
Sending a one-time email notification
UPDATE Order SET Status = 'Shipped'
Charging a credit card via an external payment gateway
questions.explain: Setting a field to a fixed value produces the same end state whether it runs once or many times. An insert, an email send, and a charge each produce a new duplicate effect every time they run.

questions.q: In the idempotency pattern shown in this lesson, what does a subscriber check before performing its non-idempotent work?
options: The event's Replay ID, used as a durable unique key
Whether the org has exceeded its daily API limit
Whether the subscribing trigger is marked as high-volume
Whether the event's EventUuid has already been recorded as processed
questions.explain: The pattern checks a tracking record (keyed on the event's EventUuid, a system-populated unique identifier for that specific message) to skip work already done, rather than relying on the Replay ID, which is a stream position, not a durable unique key.

questions.q: Within a single event channel, what ordering guarantee does Salesforce make?
options: No ordering guarantee at all, even within one channel
Ordering is only guaranteed for standard-volume events
Delivery order is preserved within a single channel, but not guaranteed across different channels or event types
Ordering is only guaranteed if Pub/Sub API is used
questions.explain: Order is preserved within a single channel's stream, but there is no platform-wide guarantee of ordering across different channels or event types — that needs an explicit sequence field if it matters.

questions.q: Why does fixing duplicate-delivery (idempotency) not automatically fix an ordering problem?
options: Because they are the same problem solved by the same fix
Because ordering problems only occur with custom platform events, never CDC
Because idempotency can only be implemented in Flow, not Apex
Because idempotency makes repeated processing of the SAME event safe, while ordering is about whether DIFFERENT, dependent events are processed in the right sequence
questions.explain: Idempotency addresses safely re-processing the same event twice; ordering is a separate concern about whether one event's effects are visible before a dependent event is processed — each needs its own explicit design fix.
